body.statement:
The event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\) imposes \(M^R=0\), \(M^0=M^\star=XZ^\top\), exact rank, blockwise uniform geometry, independent row-heteroskedastic noise, variance replication, growing-path leverage, and the primitive band-remainder envelope.  The published Choi--Yuan model-and-scalar-functional class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\) instead permits \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\) with \(M^R\ne0\), uses global incoherence and conditioning, assumes i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise, and imposes the six hypotheses of its scalar staggered-adoption Theorem 3.2.

The band-valid event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\) and the published Choi--Yuan model-and-scalar-functional class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\) are incomparable:
\[
 \mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\not\subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\not\subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}.
\]
The common class is nonempty and obeys
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}
 \subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\cap\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}.
\]
Consequently, if a coverage-frontier converse is witnessed by one array in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}\), that array is admissible for the corresponding supremum over the full published class.  In the other direction, validity of the event-transfer band does not extend by class inclusion to the full published class: a nonzero approximation component \(M^R\) contributes a bias term not present in the event-transfer remainder \(\rho_n\) and must be controlled separately.
body.proof_tex:
The two scope descriptions follow directly from \(\texttt{def:cy-event-class}\) and \(\texttt{def:published-choi-yuan-class}\) and their displayed member properties.  We now give explicit complete-array certificates for both noninclusions.
Because every fixed envelope in the event-transfer definition is positive, choose integers \(d_n\uparrow\infty\) recursively fast enough to make each of the finitely many required ratios at index \(n\) no larger than its prescribed envelope.  This diagonal choice is legitimate once the ratios below are shown to converge to zero.

For the event-transfer-only certificate, take one adopting cohort of size \(d_n\), \(d_n^2\) never-treated donors, \(K=1\), adoption at \(g=d_n^2+1\), and \(T=d_n^2+1\), and set \(\tau_{it}=0\) for every cell.  Put \(x_i=z_t=1\), so \(M^0\) has rank one, condition number one, and all block incoherence and normalized Gram eigenvalues equal one.  Let the errors be mutually independent Gaussian variables, with variance one on adopting rows and variance two on donor rows.  They are centered, row-heteroskedastic, uniformly sub-Gaussian, and bounded away from zero and infinity, but they are not identically distributed.

Here \(n_g=d_n\), \(|J_{g0}|=|S_g|=d_n^2\), and the three influence coefficients are respectively \(d_n^{-1}\) on each treated target cell, \(-d_n^{-2}\) on each donor target cell, and \(-d_n^{-3}\) on each treated pre-period cell.  Hence
\[
 s_0^2=d_n^{-1}+2d_n^{-2}+d_n^{-3},
 \qquad
 L_n(1)\le\sqrt2\,d_n^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 |\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}|\le3d_n^3. \tag{1}
\]
It follows that the leverage ratio is \(O(d_n^{-1}\log^5d_n)\).  The variance-replication ratio is \(O(d_n^{-1}\sqrt{\log d_n})\).  Since the rank-one block signal is of order \(d_n^2\), the signal, spectral-size, and missing-block ratios are respectively \(O(d_n^{-1}\sqrt{\log d_n})\), \(O(d_n^{-2}\log^3d_n)\), and \(O(d_n^{-1})\).  Direct substitution in \(R_{g0}^{\mathrm{CY}}\), followed by division by \(s_0\asymp d_n^{-1/2}\), gives
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(1)=O(d_n^{-3/2}\log d_n). \tag{2}
\]
All these quantities vanish, so the recursive choice of \(d_n\) places the array in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\).  Its two variance values violate the i.i.d. homoskedastic noise property of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\).  This proves the first noninclusion.

For the published-only certificate, use the same dimensions, adoption schedule, and zero treatment-effect array, take i.i.d. \(N(0,1)\) noise, and set
\[
 M_n^\star=\mathbf1_N\mathbf1_T^\top,
 \qquad
 M_n^R=\zeta_n w_n v_n^\top, \tag{3}
\]
where \(w_n\perp\mathbf1_N\) and \(v_n\perp\mathbf1_T\) have entries bounded by one and are nonzero.  Choose \(\zeta_n>0\) smaller than the right side of the published approximation condition and small enough that all six published scalar-functional ratios hold.  Such a positive choice exists at every finite \(n\), and it can be made to tend to zero.  The leading matrix in (3) has globally balanced rank-one singular vectors, condition number one, and satisfies the global Gram and target-loading lower bounds.  With dimensions increasing sufficiently fast, the other three published ratios vanish.  Thus the array lies in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\).  Orthogonality in (3) gives \(\operatorname{rank}(M_n^0)=2\) for every \(n\), whereas the event-transfer model fixes \(r=1\) and requires \(\operatorname{rank}(M^0)=r\).  Therefore this array is not in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), proving the second noninclusion.

Setting \(\zeta_n=0\) in (3), retaining i.i.d. homoskedastic Gaussian noise, and choosing the same dimensions recursively to satisfy both families of mapped ratios gives a member of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}\).  Hence the common class is nonempty; its two inclusions follow directly from the intersection in \(\texttt{def:cy-common-subclass}\).

If a loss or coverage shortfall is at least \(c>0\) for one law in the common class, then the supremum over the published class is at least that value because the common law is an admissible published law.  This proves upward transfer of a converse.  Conversely, neither noninclusion licenses transfer of an upper guarantee.  In particular, substituting \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\) into a counterfactual error decomposes it into the event-transfer score and remainder plus the omitted approximation contrast induced by \(M^R\); that contrast is identically zero only under \(M^R=0\).  Therefore an additional approximation-bias bound is necessary before the event-transfer upper-band theorem can cover the full published class.
body.justification: The proposition prevents the note-specific class from being mistaken for the published approximate-rank class and supplies a common domain for a transferable converse.
body.gap: Neither class contains the other because approximate rank and i.i.d. homoskedastic noise cut in opposite directions from exact rank and row heteroskedasticity.
body.consumer: Any eventual lower witness in the common subclass transfers to the published class, while upper-band claims remain confined to the event-transfer domain unless approximation bias is added.
